Hi Sasha — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard:
- ACME is prioritizing predictable latency under load and clear incident response SLAs for production inference.
- You want clear commitments around time-to-ack, RCA cadence, and support escalation paths.
- Competitive concern: how Redwood compares to hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS/GCP) on SLA + incident handling.

2) Redwood differentiators (high level):
- Dedicated routing & failover policies so you can pin a model variant and fallback automatically to cheaper/compatible variant without losing requests.
- SLA-backed Dedicated offering with defined P95/P99 latency targets and 24/7 escalation for enterprise plans.
- Tactical play: automatic KV cache warming + continuous batching reduces noisy-start latency during incidents.

3) Proposed next steps:
- Share an incident response matrix and a short SLA comparison vs AWS/GCP (attached). (Action: me — attached PDF)
- Run a short tabletop test with ACME Security to validate RCA cadence and evidence collection (target: next week). (Action: Laura to coordinate)
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min deep-dive with Vivek to walk our support + escalation runbook and sample RCA template.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-slas.pdf, rhi_incident_response_matrix.xlsx

Any gaps in the summary? If this looks good, I'll have Laura reach out to book the tabletop.

Thanks,
Rishi

Sasha — hi, Marissa here (support + escalation lead). A few notes to address your procurement/security checklist items and to be transparent about differences vs hyperscalers: 

1) Time-to-ack / escalation
- Dedicated Enterprise SLA: initial acknowledgement for Sev 1 within 15 minutes (page to on-call), primary contact assigned within 30 minutes. This is in our Dedicated SLA attachment; we can include it verbatim in contractual language.

2) Interim updates vs final RCA
- We provide an initial incident summary within 2 hours for Sev 1 (if we have partial telemetry), then scheduled interim updates every 6-8 hours until containment. Final RCA delivered within 5 business days for Sev 1, with a triage addendum within 48 hours when more evidence is required. Sample RCA template attached (sample-rca-template.docx).

3) Differentiator vs hyperscalers (practical):
- Hyperscalers often rely on broad platform SLAs but will surface long RCAs tied to multiple services; Redwood's benefit is a single-vendor incident path and model-specific RCAs (we correlate model state, KV cache, and routing decisions into the RCA).
- For customers running private/Dedicated deployments, we can do on-prem evidence collection or provide signed export packages for audits.

4) Tabletop test scope suggestion (Vivek + Laura to run):
- Scenario: sudden 5x spike to inference traffic for 20 minutes causing autoscale stress -> degrade to 95th/99th latency breach -> automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant -> manual rollback path.
- What we'll validate: detection time, automated failover timeline, time-to-ack, interim update cadence, RCA artifacts produced.

If that aligns, Laura will send an invite for Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks — I'll also attach a one-page incident response matrix for quick reference.

Marissa
Support & Escalations
Redwood Inference
